npcs.name: Wolchen
lines: Weapons and armor, an thou hast the coin. Plain and magic only. Naught rarer.
The forge is hot. What seekest thou?
Helms and shields also. Naught leaveth unpaid.
The knights ground their gates and left the cold-iron in the hill. I hammer what they hoarded. I bless naught.

npcs.name: Ysara
lines: Health and mana, freshly brewed.
I can mend thee, or sell thee the road's supply.
North is Briarwood, then the den, the chapel, the desert, and Qadren. Past that: Highmarket, the Cinder Barrens, and the Black Vault.
Call not on Zhera where I can hear it. That light cooked a parish into salt. I mend the body. I audit not the heart.

npcs.name: Ilyra
lines: I keep the gates betwixt difficulties.
The Hollow King is the key.
The north castle answereth no horn. Difficulty is a door I keep. The other doors keep themselves, and they hunger.

npcs.name: Quill
lines: My scriptorium standeth north of the square, the narrow tower with the patched slates. Seek me there. The rest of the town I do not walk. Not by daylight.
The shelves scarce keep a rite. I do, at ten thousand gold, and the price bendeth not. Ask not where I come by them. I would only tell thee something pleasant.
Slay four foes and I shall lay six tomes before thee. Thou choosest one. I choose nothing for thee. I have chosen for others, and I keep a list.
Read a tome and it stayeth with thee. Forty-five readings is the ceiling. I have known men reach for a forty-sixth. Hush. I have known nothing.
Some rites shut a door when thou openest them. Choose with care, friend. A door that closeth softly is still a door closed.
A ring sitteth with the books, of plain or magic make. Leave and return, and both shall have changed. Rare I do not sell. Rare things have owners, and owners come asking.
The oldest scripture nameth no fate, only the burden of a choice, and no promise that it saveth thee. I copied that line myself. Twice. The second time I believed it.

npcs.name: Bram
lines: The camp is the only quiet I am granted. The wood yet screameth.
I chop, that my hands may remember somewhat besides watching.
Follow the blood, if the trees begin to look the same.
Crimson eyes. If thou yet seest amber, that bear is already dead.
A miller's wife on the south bank hid her hound in the cellar. Love held three weeks. Then it spoke in her husband's voice.

npcs.name: Holt
lines: Blackwater. Ten thousand gold, and I shove off.
Night is worse out there. The risen wait not their turn.
I do not haggle.
A psalm was left in a split hull on this coast. I ferried not the hand that wrote it.

npcs.name: Myrine
lines: The skiff is Holt's. This bank is mine.
A bow whilst they are far. A spear if they forget themselves.
I slay what steppeth into my watch. The lesson I do not share.
Blackwater breatheth. I stay upon this shore.
The drowned do not bargain. Feed them not, and call it not a victory.

npcs.name: Orithya
lines: Martsirt endeth where the trees take the light. I keep that line.
I patrol this mouth of the wood. I walk not with thee.
What I drop stayeth where it fell. The experience is mine.
Come rude, and the spear is nearer than the bow.
Martsirt was pious until the floorboards drank. I keep the tree-line. I keep not the sermons.

npcs.name: Sable
lines: I stay south of the east road, in the deep briar. The wood I do not walk.
Fireball never sitteth beside Telekinesis.
Read Blood Soaked twenty times and Mercy drinketh less life, and striketh harder.
Ten thousand gold a tome. I keep also one ring, plain or magic. Never rare.
Leave the briar and return, an thou wouldst a different set.
A rite is a choice written down. Fate is a word the old books refuse to set in ink.

npcs.name: Wynn
lines: The parish burned the book of names, that the tide might forget. The tide yet delivereth them face-down.
Six of the drowned yet turn when a name is spoken. I pay in what their pockets kept. Salt, and a ribbon from a coat that hath no child.
East is the Bastion. They paint HOPE upon the gate, that the watch quit not. The paint is the only new thing there.
Southeast, before the water, a thin fog in the thorns. A small hatch. I do not go down.
South, the moor. A lantern with no hand beneath it is no welcome.
North climbeth back to Martsirt. They yet pretend a square is a world.
Father Noll prayed Zhera's fire on the drowned. It found the small sins and left a garden of salt. I sweep around them. I pray not.

npcs.name: Rusk
lines: Hope is the word we paint upon the gate, that the night watch quit not. Beneath it, the older word is scraped down to the grain.
Imps strip the beach, then the palisade. Slay five. I pay in coin and a nail pulled from the gate.
North, the bluffs. Folk go up to mourn and come down quieter than grief. Most of them come not down.
If the palisade faileth, burn the tents. Die not heroically in a doorway.
Sera seweth what the coast openeth. Odder trusteth heat. I trust paint, which is a confession.
They ground the castle shut. Let the blind knights see how far a prayer goeth when their own dead knock.

npcs.name: Sera
lines: I sew what the coast openeth. I promise not that it stayeth shut.
The well is clean. The folk who drink it are not.
Bring me the wounded. Leave me the sermons.
Blood washeth out of linen. It washeth not out of a name.
I had rather sew in the mud, at mine own pace, than be a pillar of salt before supper.

npcs.name: Odder
lines: Iron from the ridge. Salt in every hinge. Naught here stayeth bright.
I sell what shall break slower than thou wilt. Plain and magic only. Rare I do not keep.
Ask me not to bless a blade. Heat is the only prayer I trust.
If thou hearest the anvil at night, that is me, not a ghost. The ghosts do not work.
The white mountain tore down its lenses and put on iron. I kept the heat. I refused the blindfold.

npcs.name: Brine
lines: Lanterns walk the moor with nobody beneath them. I have ceased to wave.
Five shades. Snuff them. I shall pay thee with coins the tide did not want.
South, a crack in the shale. Smugglers. Then corpses. Then the crack.
If a light boweth unto thee, it is not being polite.
The parish burned the book of names. The tide kept a copy, and it readeth them with lanterns that have no hands.

npcs.name: Iskra
lines: We hung the ropes that the mourners need not jump. Most of them jumped. I keep the shoes.
The shades yet use the ropes. Cut five of them loose and the cliff is but a cliff until dusk.
North the stone faileth. The ground turneth to bile. Drink not what the fog offereth. It offereth in thine own voice.
Nobody returneth for the shoes. Thus I know they meant it.
Salt statues do not jump. The ones who still have shoes do. I keep both, and I prefer the shoes.

npcs.name: Jas
lines: We hid a ledger where the excise would not swim. The ledger grew teeth.
Imps count the crates now. Six of them, and thou mayst have what remaineth of the take.
Open not the red-banded cask. It is not wine. It was never wine.
If thou seest my brother, he is the quiet one. Quiet hath he been for a year.
The ledger grew teeth because the dark was hungry, not because we cheated a sum. Hunger careth not for arithmetic.

npcs.name: Moth
lines: This was a fen. The parish poured the dead into it when the sea grew too crowded to lie unto. The fen learned the recipe.
Keep to the planks. One step into the seep and it taketh the boot, then the name. The lamps are the only sky.
Six serpents in the bile. I pay thee to leave. That is the only honest wage in the bog.
West, a hole that breatheth. That is the Sink. It is no well. Calder went down for a purse.
If the fog speaketh in thy voice, answer not. It is practicing.
The fen learned its recipe from a parish that ran out of graves. Hunger is a patient cook.

npcs.name: Orlem
lines: Welcome to Qadren.
The east road climbeth into Highmarket. The barrens wait past that.
Vetch will gamble, an thou likest losing gold.
The clock-mages cracked the glass sky to feed their machines. What thou callest dusk is the receipt.

npcs.name: Heska
lines: The dunes forgive not.
Keep to the stone, an thou wouldst leave.
Highmarket pretendeth the desert is a rumor.
If a fog knoweth thy name, it is not weather. It is the appetite, practicing.

npcs.name: Vetch
lines: Gold in. Mystery out.
I gamble weapons, armor, and jewels. Most come up magic. Rare is three-and-twenty in a hundred. Unique, two. Plain white I do not deal.
The house usually winneth. Usually.
Once the box offered a crown that seeth by the eyes of beasts. I put it back. Some winnings eat the winner.

npcs.name: Hask
lines: The ridge taketh a toll in ankles. Mine I take in coin.
Maulers camp upon the turns. Five of them, and the switchbacks are only steep.
Up is the Ascent. The air there is thin enough to lie unto thee.
If thou slip, grab not a root. The roots here are fingers.
Cold-iron was hoarded up the mountain, then the gates were ground shut. Down here the toll is still ankles.

npcs.name: Calder
lines: I came down for a coin purse. The purse was a jaw. I stay upon the lip, that the pool get not a new face.
Four eyeless things dwell in the bile. Slay them, then leave. Tell Moth I am not coming up.
If the bile toucheth thee, wipe it not upon thy mouth. It seeketh a way in.
There is one stair. It is not for me.
I came for a purse. The purse was a jaw because the ground is a stomach. Tell that to no saint. Saints pour water on it.

npcs.name: Cal
lines: The ring without the plaza is no market. It is a grave.
Gideon cleared crypts by feeding them his own, then came out a hero. I pay for dead callers. I pay not for that hero.

npcs.name: Pell
lines: Highmarket buyeth, selleth, and pretendeth the wall is enough.
East is the Cinder Barrens. North of those rocks is the Black Vault.
If thou camest from Qadren, thou knowest already the desert lieth.
The north castle answereth no horn. We ring our own bells, that the town may sound larger than its graves.

npcs.name: Nim
lines: The wind up here repeateth whatever thou wert about to confess.
Pilgrims begin laughing and cease not. Six of those laughers. Then the pass is only cold.
West, the crypts are drowning. East, the iron gate yet pretendeth it is a border.
I was bound for the spires. I stay where the air yet answereth.
The wind repeateth confessions because the stone below is collecting them. Laugh not with it. The laugh doth not end.

npcs.name: Sarn
lines: The maulers charge any who useth the road.
The north arch is the Black Vault. I go not in.
An ash-camp saint sold a beautiful lie out in the cinders. His water was the sickness, watered thin. I host no saints.

npcs.name: Vellum
lines: The names upon the slabs washed off. The dead took that personally.
Callers stand in the water and read the blanks. Put four of them down.
North droppeth into the chasm. What the crypts lose, the chasm keepeth.
If a coffin be already open, it was not me. It was the tide.
The slabs are blank because the stone hath begun to breathe. A name is a meal it already took.

npcs.name: Kell
lines: This gate held a kingdom. Then the kingdom began charging its own dead a toll.
Maulers wear our tabards now. Six of them, and the arch is only stone again.
East is the Inquisitor's gaol. He locked the faithful in and forgot which side of the door he stood upon.
I yet have the key. It openeth nothing. I keep it that my hand may have a labor.
They hoarded the cold-iron and ground the gates. The tabards on the dead are the answer their prayers received.

npcs.name: Lute
lines: I dove for a bell. The bell ringeth yet, and I am yet here.
Shades crowd the span. Five of them. Then the dark may have the rest.
Look not into the pool long enough to recognize a face.
If I follow thee out, wait not. I shall not make the stairs.
There is a glass that showeth not thy face, but the ancestor whose sin thou art paying. I dove for a bell. I look not in glass.

npcs.name: Piet
lines: The Inquisitor bade us confess a sin he had not yet invented. We did our best.
The risen yet wear our irons. Eight of them. Then this floor may be a ruin, and not a sermon.
North, the chapel yet playeth itself. Past that, the trees eat the sun.
If thou findest him, bring him not back. Mercy was his word. He used it as a nail.
Every confession spoken in this gaol is still in the air. Stand in it long, and a stranger's sin shall sit upon thy chest.

npcs.name: Ors
lines: The spires were a church until the roots decided they were pews. The canopy voted, and the sun lost.
One thing walketh in the clearing. It weareth a bear as a man weareth a stolen coat. Slay it. I shall melt the Inquisitor's silver.
Leave not the road. The trees argue with aught that doth, and they raise not their voices.
Already have I been wrong in there once. I will not go in to be wrong a second time.
The ring of black glass is the lair. Act I endeth under the lid. The road is the only honest thing in it.
The Crow-King entereth by iron crowns and old sins, and then it taketh the memory of speech. I have a bear to worry. The crown may wait.

npcs.name: Holt
lines: The way back is paid.
Blackwater stayeth not dead. Slay what riseth, else it keepeth rising.
The bilge of a wreck keepeth a psalm. I charge for the crossing. The psalm chargeth for the singing.
